chapters.title: Chapter 4040: Oh, Order! III
paragraphs: After such a phenomenal change, Noah took a moment to reflect on the terrifying distinction he had received.
He also looked at Sigrid, studying her transformed state with perception that could now see deeper than before.

The more he observed, the more he noticed something concerning...her eyes were getting brighter and brighter, the silver-white light within them intensifying with each passing second. The illumination didn’t seem entirely... hers.
"Sigrid."
He called out calmly, his voice cutting through whatever was building within her. The foreign white light of majesty in her eyes dimmed somewhat, like a tide pulling back from shore.
She blinked, focusing on him with what seemed like tremendous effort, as if anchoring herself to his presence.

"Do not worry," she said, though her smile carried edges of something vast trying to express itself through limited form. "I am still... me. But I am receiving an inflow of... information. Of possibilities. Of Order."
She spoke while trying to study her own existence, her hands moving as if she could grasp the changes occurring within her.
"Come."
A single word from Noah, but his voice carried magnetic authority that transcended simple command. Sigrid floated toward him without conscious thought, drawn by forces that operated below awareness.
When she reached him, Noah took her in his arms with careful certainty, placing his forehead against hers in a gesture both intimate and analytical.
He closed his eyes and extended his perception, sensing both their existences simultaneously.
What he felt defied simple description!
Order coursed through them both like a white river of liquid law, drenching every cell, every meridian, every pathway.

His Towers of Osmont, those impossible structures that grew within his being, were being bathed in Order’s light. The flow wasn’t violent or overwhelming...it was inexorable, like gravity asserting itself, like mathematics proving theorems.
Everything was being touched by Order. Everything was being... corrected.
|Due to Order rising and flowing within your Existence, all established Living Existential Authorities have been effectively contained within your being.|
|This tremendous elevation has distinguished you beyond standard classification.|
|You are no longer merely an Early Creature.|
|You have been distinguished as: The Early Creature, Osmont|
HUUM!
The distinction hit him with a glorious weight.
Not "an" Early Creature...that was too common, too limited.
Not "THE Creature"...that was far too vast, a title belonging to something that transcended current understanding.
He was now The Early Creature, Osmont. Unique. Specified. Recognized by existence itself as something particular and irreplaceable.
|With your liberated Fear and Doubt alongside the elevation of your distinctions due to thr inclusion of Order:|
|All future completed Towers of Osmont at Stage 1 will grant 6.5 Million Complexity and Purity.|
|All 159 forged Towers that have crossed Stage 1 receive retroactive correction.|
|Retroactive bonus applied: +1,033,500,000 Complexity and Purity.|
The number was staggering, but more prompts continued to cascade!
|All Towers of Osmont achieving Stage 2 now grant 25 Million Complexity and Purity|
|Retroactive correction for previously completed Stage 2 Towers applied|
|Additional bonus: +775,000,000 Complexity and Purity|
|Due to corrective changes from Order’s influence, Total gains of 1,808,500,000 Complexity and Purity have been granted.|
|Current Total Complexity: 4,576,473,891|
|Current Total Purity: 4,575,892,734|
Noah read through the prompts while simultaneously feeling the changes ripple through his existence.
His Towers of Osmont grew larger, more ancient, their crystalline structures taking on qualities that suggested they had always existed.

The Early Atlas of the Folds rumbled within him, its pathways becoming more complex as Order flowed through its structure, creating new routes to the Earliest Folds that hadn’t existed moments before.
But it was his Heart that experienced the most dramatic change.
|The Heart of The Early Creature, Osmont, is utilizing this burst of complexity to achieve completion of its Second Part|
|Oruvian Shardveil - The Arterial Convergence Core: COMPLETE|
|Blood production dramatically increased|
|10,000 Drops of Blood of The Early Creature, Osmont, have been generated simultaneously!|
|Current blood generation rate: 1,000 drops per hour.|
These were just his changes...significant, transformative, revolutionary!
But Sigrid, as THE Living Order, was undergoing something that transcended normal advancement entirely!
With their foreheads still connected, Noah could sense the explosion of growth within her.
His enhanced perception, now backed by the authority of THE Living Existential Guider, allowed him to tap into her existence and quantify the boons she was receiving.
What he saw made even his fearless, doubtless mind pause in awe.
|Sigrid, THE Living Order, is undergoing existential correction|
|Her being is aligning with what Order truly means, with her existence correcting to live upto its breadth.|
|Current rate of increase: 1,000,000,000 Complexity and Purity per second|
|Duration: Ongoing|
|Estimated completion: Unknown|
Oh.
Oh!!!
A billion in Complexity and Purity. Per second!
The mathematics were staggering. If this continued for just one hundred seconds, she would stand among Honored Living Existences in pure numerical terms.
But would it stop there? As she was becoming THE Living Order...not just representing it but embodying it, would the correction simply continue? Would it decrease? Accelerate?
And when it finally stopped, what power would she possess?
Because she wasn’t just any Living Existence now!
She carried the designation THE. Capitalized. Absolute! Fucking bolded!
Recognized by existence itself as not just an example of Order, but Order’s own consciousness given form.
THE Living Order.

In the Earliest Folds, Noah remembered how just witnessing THE Living Spirit had given a Fold Dweller immense honor, as most beings couldn’t even perceive such entities. They existed at frequencies of reality that transcended normal observation.
What did it mean for someone to become one of these esteemed beings? To not just wield their authority but to be their authority?
Noah’s eyes blazed with tyrannical interest as he maintained the connection, watching complexity flow into Sigrid at rates that would have destroyed any normal being.
But she wasn’t normal. She never had been. And now, guided by his distinction and freed from her Disorder, she was becoming what she had always been meant to be!
As he remained connected with her, he marveled how all of this stemmed from her losing her memory, crashing in the Veiled Sunfolds, and his connection with Kalysta bringing him to her.

chapters.title: Chapter 4041: Oh, Order! IV
paragraphs: Thinking of this reminded him of the Primarchs and Masters of Existence of the Veiled Sunfolds. Entanglements and connections. He wouldn’t entirely forget them as there was much to do!
Noah refocused on Sigrid.
He wished he had the seconds to count everything as Sigrid’s complexity exploded beyond comprehension.
Each heartbeat that passed represented billions in advancement, each breath she took rewrote the glory of what power meant.
But even as a few seconds passed...three billion, four billion, five billion with each tick of time, his expression shifted from wonder to something heavier.

Without warning, he disconnected from Sigrid’s forehead, the loss of that intimate connection leaving a cold space between them. His gaze turned outward, piercing through the twisted corridors of the Doorway toward the distant exit that lay beyond the winding pathways.
Something was wrong.
Or rather, something was about to become very complicated.
In another region entirely, within the Transcendent Origin Battlefront Folds, deep in the protected depths of Aeternitas Concordia, space tore itself apart to admit Duke Gwendolyn’s form.
She materialized within the domed garden with such haste that reality hadn’t quite caught up, her edges still blurring as she solidified before Noah’s merchant body.

"What happened in the Doorway?!" Her usual composure had cracked, revealing genuine alarm beneath. "The Young Miss awakened?! You all must make a quick exit...the white rays of Order have spread across the Doorway and towards the entirety of the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds!"
She moved closer, her stellar dark hair whipping with the force of her urgency.

"Teleportation or warping across Folds isn’t possible from within a Doorway...you must exit first. Turn back as quickly as possible! My clone will try to keep the commotion around the Doorway covered as much as I can, but..." Her expression grew heavier with each word. "You must exit the Doorway!"
Noah’s eyes flashed with sharp understanding. Order had permeated across the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds as a consequence of Sigrid’s awakening.
Such a phenomenon wouldn’t go unnoticed. It couldn’t go unnoticed. Every Paradox in existence would feel Order reasserting itself, even if they did not fully know or understand what it was!
"I’ve already alerted Duke Whisker and others..."
Duke Gwendolyn’s words cut through his calculations, and Noah’s gaze turned sharp enough to cut dimensions.
His voice emerged with distaste that he didn’t bother to hide.
"Of course you have." The words dripped with contempt. "You truly like to talk and share absolutely everything, don’t you?"
HUUM!
Duke Gwendolyn’s expression turned stern, her diplomatic mask reasserting itself with visible effort. "For the sake of the Young Miss, yes. I will not play word games with you."

She straightened, authority radiating from her form. "Take her out. Reinforcements will come toward the entrance of that doorway. What I know for certain is that soon it will be surrounded by Paradoxes, and I alone cannot ensure her safety against multiple Dukes of Paradox."
She paused, letting the weight of the situation settle before continuing.
"With reinforcements, we shall take the Young Miss back here or to the Heart of Origin where the Kleos Council is. There, we can ensure her protection."
Noah gazed at Gwendolyn with eyes that had grown colder than the space between stars.

Internally, his mind rejected every word she spoke. Sigrid taken by them? Brought back here to be protected like some fragile treasure? Taken to the Heart of Origin to be displayed and discussed and controlled?
Like he would allow such a thing to happen.
His mind buzzed with possibilities, plans forming and reforming at speeds that would have been impossible if doubt still clouded his thoughts.
Duke Gwendolyn rose into the air, and in the next moment, reality acknowledged her authority as multiple tears in space unfolded within the domed garden.
Powerful Duke-level existences stepped through...Duke Whisker among them, his tiny form radiating power that belied his size.
Duke Pyralis emerged in flames that froze the air. Duke Valen tapped through with his cane, blind eyes seeing more than sight allowed!
Others followed, more than a dozen Dukes answering her call with speed that suggested prior preparation.

Duke Gwendolyn looked over the assembled power with satisfaction that she couldn’t quite hide. "The mission is a dangerous one...venturing into the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds for the retrieval of something too precious to lose. I will act as the anchor to take you all directly there at thr shortest possible time."

Her existence erupted into white-gold light that formed a massive arched gateway. She stood at its center, her very being becoming the pathway that would allow traversal across countless distances between Folds. The gateway hummed with authority that made space itself bow!

Duke Whisker scurried through without delay, his small form disappearing into the light...but his gaze was cloudy. Before he disappeared, he turned towards Noah, and Noah stared back at him calmly as this little mouse of a Duke...seemed contemplative!
Others followed quickly, understanding that time was not their ally in this matter.
Noah watched this phenomenon with cold calculation, his own plans already forming in the spaces between their assumptions.
Meanwhile, in a place that existed perpendicular to normal reality, inside a certain mountain surrounded by Living Conceptual Authority.
In the Ethereal Summit of Unspoken Truths...Duke Valen’s other body stroked his beard thoughtfully.
"Gwendolyn seems to have boldly taken the Vessel of THE Living Order into the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds," he announced to the gathering of beings whose power transcended normal classification.
"She is now undergoing an awakening inside a Doorway."
His blind gaze fixed on Schrodinger specifically, seeing him in ways that eyes never could.
"You will soon have visitors in your Transcendent Paradoxical Folds."
Schrodinger’s smile bloomed like a paradox...both genuine and calculating, warm and terrifying.

"Oh, I was just about to begin tracking the origin of the white rays of light spreading across the Paradoxical Folds. Since you’re going there now, give me the exact coordinates. I could use this to our advantage before the Kleos Concordat."
The casual way he spoke of manipulating events that could reshape existence made even these ancient beings pause!

chapters.title: Chapter 4042: Oh, Order! V
paragraphs: Duke Valen nodded, beginning to transmit information to Schrodinger.
A terrifying Living Quantum, its form existing in seventeen states simultaneously...turned toward them with attention that made probability itself pay notice. "What do you plan to do?"
Schrodinger’s smile deepened, containing layers of meaning that contradicted themselves at every level. "I plan to display a show of force... and then a show of mercy."
HUUM!
He stood, his beggar’s robes somehow managing to convey majesty despite their tattered state.

"You see, sometimes after a display of overwhelming force...after showing what devastation could be unleashed, what horror could be made manifest, showing mercy instead makes others breathe such deep sighs of relief that they actually thank you. They thank you for not destroying them, for showing restraint, for being merciful. They forget that you shouldn’t have threatened them in the first place. They’re so grateful for what didn’t happen that they overlook what did."
His smile grew mysterious, containing paradoxes within paradoxes.
"I plan to get... a thank you, that’s all."
The others on the mountain shook their heads...some with multiple heads, some with concepts that served as heads.
A Living Dimensional, whose voice existed in frequencies that created their own spaces, boomed out a warning.
"Don’t make things too crazy before the Kleos Concordat."
Schrodinger smiled and said nothing, but his eyes were already seeing something else entirely.
Those eyes...windows into paradox itself, contained layers that defied observation.

One moment they were watching and observing others on this mountain, seeing them in the present, in the past, in futures that might never be. The next moment, they were observing the vast Transcendent Paradoxical Folds, seeing through space and time as if such divisions were merely suggestions.
His body in the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds had those same mysterious eyes.
His beggar-like figure stood surrounded by waves of obsidian-gold paradox that made reality uncertain about whether he existed or not.
He took a single step...just one, and space folded around the simplicity of the action.
BOOM!
His terrifying aura manifested near the entrance of a certain Doorway to the Loom with the casualness of someone who had always been there.
He observed calmly as Duke Gwendolyn’s Paradoxical body watched the blazing white rays of Order blooming from the Doorway with barely contained panic.
Her attention shifted, drawn by the weight of his presence, and her veiled face turned toward him.
Even through the veil, her expression was readable...shock transforming into something approaching horror as she recognized who had appeared.
Schrodinger looked at her veiled face with a smile that contained genuine amusement.

He laughed internally, knowing she must be wondering how he had arrived so quickly. How he had known exactly where to appear. How he had crossed distances that should have taken seconds or a minute in less than a heartbeat.
’Silly girl,’ he thought with something approaching fondness. ’You told me even without knowing. You... might as well have sent me an invitation.’
He shook his head at her naivety, finding it almost endearing that someone so astute could be so blind to certain realities.

It was a wonder that both she and he carried the distinction of Dukes. If all Dukes thought like her...linearly, obviously, predictably, how different the vast Folds would be. How fucked the Folds would be!
How much simpler. How much more boring.
He saw the blooming white-gold portal beside her, recognizing the pathway through which Duke Valen and the others would soon arrive.
Reinforcements rushing to protect THE Living Order, to secure her, to control her resurrection.
But he didn’t attack.
As he had told the others, he was here for a show of force... and then mercy.
He smiled and nodded toward Gwendolyn with the politeness of someone acknowledging a neighbor. Then, with the casual air of someone calling friends to dinner, he snapped his fingers.
BOOM!

Space trembled paradoxically, reality trying to decide whether it should break or bend. One terrifying aura of Duke-level Paradox began to appear, then another, then another, each arrival making existence less certain about its own rules.

Duke Elagabalus materialized first, his form a contradiction of youth and ancient age that hurt to perceive directly. Duke Diviticus emerged from nothing, her presence making the air itself question whether it existed.
More followed...two dozen Dukes of Paradox, each one a violation of what should be possible!
HUUM!
They looked toward the brilliant light of Order emanating from the Doorway with expressions of distaste, as if the brightness itself was offensive to their nature.
Because it was trying to make their existences... ordered. Trying to impose structure on beings that existed specifically because structure shouldn’t apply to them.
It was a violation. An insult. A challenge that could not go unanswered!

In addition to the Dukes, hundreds of Honored Living Paradoxes began to appear, their forms filling the space around the Doorway like an army of impossibilities. Each one radiated power that could unmake Prime Living Existences with casual thought.
In the distance, Duke Gwendolyn’s face...even veiled, visibly paled with shock and horror.
She stood alone before all this!

The reinforcements she had called for hadn’t even arrived yet, and already she was outnumbered twenty to one. The white-gold portal beside her seemed suddenly fragile, a candle flame before a hurricane of paradox.
Schrodinger stood at the center of it all, his beggar’s appearance doing nothing to diminish the terrible authority he commanded.
He had arranged this...all of it, with a few words and perfect timing.
Now came the interesting part.
The show of force was here.
Then would be the mercy that would make them grateful for what he didn’t do!
As he hummed to himself, the white gold portal beside Duke Gwendolyn shone brightly as one powerful Living Origin after another began to come out.
Each was at the level of a Duke, but as they appeared, all the expressions were changing one by one as what they were coming into was so horrendous, that one could easily mistake it for a trap.
All around, they were surrounded by living paradoxes- more than twice a dozen Dukes of Paradox as they were double their number!

How he had known exactly where to appear.
How he had crossed distances that should have taken seconds or a minute in less than a heartbeat.
’Silly girl,’ he thought with something approaching fondness. ’You told me even without knowing.
You... might as well have sent me an invitation.’
He shook his head at her naivety, finding it almost endearing that someone so astute could be so blind to certain realities.
It was a wonder that both she and he carried the distinction of Dukes.
If all Dukes thought like her...linearly, obviously, predictably, how different the vast Folds would be.
How fucked the Folds would be!
How much simpler.
How much more boring.
He saw the blooming white-gold portal beside her, recognizing the pathway through which Duke Valen and the others would soon arrive.
Reinforcements rushing to protect THE Living Order, to secure her, to control her resurrection.
But he didn’t attack.
As he had told the others, he was here for a show of force... and then mercy.
He smiled and nodded toward Gwendolyn with the politeness of someone acknowledging a neighbor.
Then, with the casual air of someone calling friends to dinner, he snapped his fingers.
BOOM!
Space trembled paradoxically, reality trying to decide whether it should break or bend.
One terrifying aura of Duke-level Paradox began to appear, then another, then another, each arrival making existence less certain about its own rules.
Duke Elagabalus materialized first, his form a contradiction of youth and ancient age that hurt to perceive directly.
Duke Diviticus emerged from nothing, her presence making the air itself question whether it existed.
More followed...two dozen Dukes of Paradox, each one a violation of what should be possible!
HUUM!
They looked toward the brilliant light of Order emanating from the Doorway with expressions of distaste, as if the brightness itself was offensive to their nature.
Because it was trying to make their existences... ordered.
Trying to impose structure on beings that existed specifically because structure shouldn’t apply to them.
It was a violation.
An insult.
A challenge that could not go unanswered!
In addition to the Dukes, hundreds of Honored Living Paradoxes began to appear, their forms filling the space around the Doorway like an army of impossibilities.
Each one radiated power that could unmake Prime Living Existences with casual thought.
In the distance, Duke Gwendolyn’s face...even veiled, visibly paled with shock and horror.
She stood alone before all this!
The reinforcements she had called for hadn’t even arrived yet, and already she was outnumbered twenty to one.
The white-gold portal beside her seemed suddenly fragile, a candle flame before a hurricane of paradox.
Schrodinger stood at the center of it all, his beggar’s appearance doing nothing to diminish the terrible authority he commanded.
He had arranged this...all of it, with a few words and perfect timing.
Now came the interesting part.
The show of force was here.
Then would be the mercy that would make them grateful for what he didn’t do!
As he hummed to himself, the white gold portal beside Duke Gwendolyn shone brightly as one powerful Living Origin after another began to come out.
Each was at the level of a Duke, but as they appeared, all the expressions were changing one by one as what they were coming into was so horrendous, that one could easily mistake it for a trap.
All around, they were surrounded by living paradoxes- more than twice a dozen Dukes of Paradox as they were double their number!

chapters.title: Chapter 4043: Force and Mercy! I
paragraphs: Schrodinger observed with the patience of someone who had witnessed the birth and death of paradoxes themselves as one Duke of Living Origins after another emerged from the white-gold portal beside Duke Gwendolyn.

His smile grew with each arrival, and he looked upon their faces individually, studying them with the intensity of someone greeting long-lost friends...if those friends happened to be beings he might destroy with a thought.
His gaze was eerie in its calmness, each glance containing layers of paradoxical power that made reality uncertain about whether it should allow him to exist.
When the last Duke had emerged and they stood arrayed before the encirclement of Paradoxes with their faces heavy, the Paradoxes and Origins looked at each other!
Nobody spoke!
Duke Whisker had a chilly expression as he looked around the encirclement, eventually coming to stop his gaze on the entity that looked like a beggar...Schrodinger.
As if many knew who the seat of power here truly was.
In this tense face off, it felt stifling for even Dukes to voice out anything.
And yet, in such an environment, a begger stepped forward as behind him, many paradoxes pulsed!
Schrodinger floated forward calmly as if he were taking a stroll as he...began to speak.
"When I was a boy..." His voice carried waves of terrific power.

He floated upward slightly, his tattered robes billowing despite the absence of wind. "A tiny little paradox that barely knew anything about existence or my place within it, I found myself running from some of the first Mutated Inevitabilities that had ever risen."
He moved as he spoke, drifting through the air with movements that seemed random yet purposeful.

"I was tired. Worn to the very edge of dissolution. My paradoxical nature was unraveling from the strain of maintaining coherence while fleeing." He raised one hand casually, and every Paradox behind him froze in perfect stillness, understanding the gesture as absolute command to remain motionless while he alone moved forward!

"In my desperation, I came across a garden. Not just any garden, but the garden of a particularly terrifying Fold Dweller. Now, you might wonder...how could a Fold Dweller be terrifying to a Living Paradox?" He chuckled, the sound containing contradictions. "This one was different. His garden existed in ways that made even paradox feel like nothing..."
HUUM!

Schrodinger drifted closer to Duke Gwendolyn and the others, his approach casual, unthreatening...a simple beggar floating through space. Yet each inch he drew nearer made the Living Origins tense further, his carefree demeanor somehow more menacing than any display of power.

"I looked toward this Fold Dweller with desperation that transcended pride. I asked...begged really, whether I could enter his garden for protection against the Mutated Inevitabilities." He paused, letting the image settle. "The Fold Dweller considered me for a moment that lasted eternity and no time at all. Then he nodded."
His voice grew warmer, as if recalling a fond memory.

"I entered the periphery of his garden, and I was actually safe. Shockingly, miraculously, the Inevitabilities could not pass through into that space. They raged at the borders, they threw themselves against barriers they couldn’t perceive, but they could not enter. It was... marvelous."
Schrodinger’s expression shifted, growing more complex.

"Seconds later...and I mean this literally, mere seconds, ten Living Existences came from another direction. They too were being chased by Mutated Inevitabilities, their forms showing the strain of extended flight." He gestured expansively. "The moment they saw the garden, saw my figure and the Fold Dweller within it, they were ecstatic. Without pause, without thought, without asking, they rushed in for protection."
He stopped directly in front of the entrance to the Doorway and Duke Gwendolyn’s portal, positioning himself alone before all these Living Origins!

"Once again, the Inevitabilities could not enter. These Living Existences...Origin, Temporal, even a young Concept among them...breathed such deep sighs of relief. They looked toward the Fold Dweller to thank him for his sanctuary, for his protection, for saving their existences."
Schrodinger’s smile grew sharp.

"Yet in the next moment, the Fold Dweller took a common farming tool...nothing special, just a hoe he used for tending his plants, and swatted down." He made a casual gesture, as if brushing away dust.
"The weavings of existence of those Living Existences were decimated instantly. All of them. Dead before they could process what was happening."
The silence that followed was absolute. Even the white rays of Order streaming from the Doorway seemed to dim slightly.

"The Fold Dweller looked at all of this as calmly as if he hadn’t done anything more significant than pulling weeds. And I, out of an overabundance of curiosity that even then defined my nature, asked him- Why? Why did you kill those Living Existences and not me?"
Schrodinger’s eyes...those windows into paradox, fixed on Duke Gwendolyn with intensity that made her paradoxical body shiver despite its nature.

"The Fold Dweller turned to me with eyes that had seen the birth of concepts themselves. He said, ’This is my home. You asked for permission to enter. You are a guest.’ He gestured to the corpses that were already being absorbed by his garden’s soil. ’Those who entered afterward were merely intruders. It matters not who they are or what they are...all those intruding in my home have to die.’"
The beggar-like figure completed his circuit, now floating directly before the entrance to the Doorway, his position both casual and absolutely deliberate.
"A simple distinction. Guest or intruder. Permission or presumption. The difference between salvation and annihilation."
He looked at Duke Gwendolyn and the others, his gaze lingering on each face with the weight of evaluation. When his eyes found Duke Valen among them, his smile grew genuinely warm.

"All Living Existences will soon be meeting in the Kleos Concordat. The Living Paradoxes have no problems at all inviting other Living Existences as guests into our Paradoxical Folds." His voice carried reasonable hospitality. "But you all did not come here as guests. You did not even ask for permission."
The temperature...if such a thing existed in the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds, seemed to drop.

"You are here, currently, as intruders." He tilted his head with curiosity that contained threat. "What shall be done? Should we follow the guidance of that Fold Dweller and his treatment of guests versus intruders?"

chapters.title: Chapter 4044: Force and Mercy! II
paragraphs: The weight of his words pressed against consciousness itself.
The assembled Living Origins stood frozen, most only able to meet his gaze!
The army of Paradoxes behind him remained perfectly still, awaiting a single gesture that would transform this confrontation into catastrophe.
Into the suffocating silence, a small figure stepped forward.
Duke Whisker emerged from among the Living Origins, his tiny mouse form radiating dignity that transcended size.
His stellar eyes met Schrodinger’s paradoxical gaze without flinching, and when he spoke, his voice carried the weight of eons of accumulated wisdom.
"It seems that we are at fault for intruding." The admission was delivered without shame or fear, simply acknowledging reality.
"We will simply take our people and leave."

Schrodinger’s smile bloomed with genuine pleasure at the response. "Your people?" He gestured toward the assembled Dukes. "I see you all here... but could you mean the ones inside this Doorway? The ones among whom is someone exuding all these rays of light that paint my Folds with...Order? Is it Order? It cannot possibly be Order, right?"
HUUM!
Immense silence settled over the gathering.
Schrodinger adopted an obviously contemplative expression, as if wrestling with a difficult decision.
Finally, he sighed with theatrical weariness.

"Hey, aren’t we all striving through existence together?" His tone shifted to something almost friendly. "How about this, we won’t make any... moves. Your people can come out and leave freely. For the sake of the coming Kleos Concordat, The Living Paradoxes will let this indiscretion slide."
He spread his hands in a gesture of magnanimity.

"We are all on the same side after all, right?" His gaze shifted to fix directly on Duke Gwendolyn’s paradoxical body. "You all even have a Living Paradox on your side, which I haven’t even focused on at this time."
Duke Whisker’s expression remained neutral, but others among the Living Origins showed visible discomfort at this observation.
The implications were clear...Schrodinger could have made this about betrayal, about a Paradox siding with Origins. He was choosing not to.
In the heavy atmosphere that followed, in that prolonged silence where possibility and probability held their breath, the Living Origin body of Duke Gwendolyn stepped forward.
Her usually controlled features showed something that might have been somberness mixed with understanding as she looked toward Schrodinger.
"Thank you."
Two words.
Thank you!
Simple. Direct. Exactly what he had wanted.
He was given his thank you!
Schrodinger nodded lightly, the gesture containing satisfaction that transcended simple pleasure.
His attention turned toward the Doorway, and following his lead, every eye...stellar, paradoxical, conceptual...fixed on that entrance.

The white rays of Order still streamed forth, painting large swaths of the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds with light that made Paradox uncomfortable. Whatever was causing that phenomenon would have to emerge soon.
Ten seconds passed.
Twenty seconds passed in absolute silence! No one moved. No one spoke. The tension grew with each heartbeat that some of them still possessed.
Then...
WAP!
Figures emerged from the Doorway.
Two figures. Only two.
The fairy form of Thessaly came first, her wings trembling as she took in the scene before her. Behind her, Altheon emerged with the careful movements of someone expecting attack from any direction.
Both paled to shades that shouldn’t have been possible for their forms as they observed the encirclement of Paradoxes, the gathered Dukes of Origin, the weight of attention focused on them.
Duke Gwendolyn waited one second. Two. Her expression shifted through confusion to alarm as she fought to maintain her composure.
"Where is the Young Miss?!"

The question cracked through the silence like breaking crystal. Yes, where was she? Where was THE Living Order whose awakening had painted the Folds with white light? Where was the being they had all come to secure?

Altheon and Thessaly stood dazed, still processing the scene before them. It was Altheon who finally managed to speak, his words emerging hesitant and confused as he looked at the encirclement of Paradoxes.
"She... left with... him."
Him.
Him!
The single word landed among the gathering with the weight of impossibility. Every being present analyzed it and its sentance differently, parsed its implications through their own understanding.
Who was ’him’?
How had they left? What did leaving even mean in this context?
The implications were staggering. They had left...suggesting they hadn’t needed to exit the Doorway to traverse across existence.
But such a thing was impossible. It was well-known, established as fundamental law, that nothing could cross or teleport across existence while within Doorways to the Loom.

Thessaly’s mental message then echoed out and reached only the Dukes of Living Origins, her hesitation palpable even in thought: "The Young Miss disappeared with... him. As if they had teleported or traversed into different Folds entirely."
The impossibility had supposedly occurred.
Into the shocked silence, Schrodinger’s voice rang out with amusement that contained layers of meaning.

"Haha, did you all lose someone important as we talked here? That must not feel so good." He drifted higher, looking down at them with sympathy. "Traversal while within a Doorway to the Loom? That should be an impossibility, and yet it has seemingly occurred..."
His expression grew helpful, concerned.
"Origin friends, do you need help looking through this Doorway to check where this... Young Miss you mention might be? Us Paradoxes should be of great help in such a search."
Origin friends? Origin friends?! What the fuck was this beggar even saying now?!
Duke Gwendolyn and others turned ashen at the offer..help from Paradoxes in finding THE Living Order would come with prices they couldn’t afford to pay.
Duke Whisker’s response was immediate and commanding, his tiny paw waving to the other Dukes with authority that transcended his size.
"We will be okay without your help."
Even as he spoke, Duke Gwendolyn and several other Dukes moved toward Thessaly and Altheon, preparing to enter the Doorway themselves to ascertain what had actually occurred.
They grabbed the two witnesses with movements that suggested interrogation would begin the moment they were out of sight!

Schrodinger watched this scene with the satisfaction of someone whose plan had executed perfectly. His gaze lingered on Duke Whisker, who had stayed back with a few others to maintain the pretense of dignity in retreat.
The beggar-like Paradox waved his hands harmlessly, as if shooing away concerns, and floated backward toward the encirclement of Living Paradoxes.

He came to rest before all the Dukes of Paradox, their forms creating a wall of impossibility that would remain as long as necessary. They would simply observe the Living Origins with menacing patience, waiting to see what panic might drive them to do.
After all, Schrodinger had gotten his thank you.
The show of force had been displayed. The mercy had been granted.
And now THE Living Order was missing, vanished through impossible means, leaving only questions and the taste of failure in the mouths of those who had come to claim her!

chapters.title: Chapter 4045: Variation! I
paragraphs: Limitations are peculiar things. They exist not as universal truths but as boundaries defined by perspective, capability, and understanding.
What one being calls impossible, another accomplishes with a casual gesture. What requires eons of preparation for some happens in heartbeats for others!
The wall that stops a child is merely a step for an adult. The ocean that drowns a man is home to a fish. The void that kills most beings is where others are born.
It was known and established...written into the fundamental understanding of existence itself, that one could not teleport in or out of the Doorways to the Loom.

This wasn’t merely difficult or dangerous; it was deemed impossible. The Doorways existed in states that rejected standard spatial manipulation, their paradoxical nature creating barriers that even Dukes couldn’t breach through normal means.
Everyone knew this. Everyone accepted this.
But Noah had never been everyone.
Seconds ago, while Duke Gwendolyn’s panic painted the air with urgency, while she urged him to make a quick exit so they could flee properly once outside the Doorway, Noah had done something simpler.
He hadn’t asked whether it was possible. He hadn’t considered the established limitations.
He had simply connected to his Early Veiled Shore.
The connection flowed through him like water remembering its source, natural and inevitable.

His brilliant energy...containing eleven Living Existential Authorities that shouldn’t coexist within a single being, pulsed with quiet certainty. The terrifying Kleos Glyph on his forehead, The Creature’s First Lesson, blazed with light that made reality pay attention.
He looked towards Sigrid and Titan!
"Are you ready to visit my home?" he had asked calmly, as if inviting them for tea rather than attempting the impossible.
Titano’s massive head had nodded with his characteristic blank expression, processing the question at his own pace.
Sigrid, still radiating the overwhelming presence of newly awakened Order, had simply nodded, her trust in him absolute despite not understanding what he intended.
Brilliant light had erupted around them...not harsh or violent, but encompassing, like being wrapped in starlight.

The illumination contained within it the authority of someone who didn’t just bend rules. He wrote new ones! Noah, Sigrid, and Titano were enveloped in radiance that made the Doorway’s paradoxical nature irrelevant.
Then they were simply... gone.
He had left Thessaly and Altheon behind without a second thought. Their baggage wasn’t something he needed to carry!
Let them explain to Duke Gwendolyn how the impossible had occurred. Let them wrestle with questions that had answers they couldn’t comprehend!
The transition was seamless, like stepping from one room to another when both rooms happened to be separated by impossible distances and fundamental barriers.
Noah, Sigrid, and Titano materialized on the golden sands of the Early Veiled Shore, the light of this impossible space welcoming them with warmth that transcended temperature!
The body of Noah that had traveled with them, one of his many simultaneous existences...became a streak of light that merged with his primary form.
He rose from where he had been seated on the sands, his upper body bare, muscles glistening with the particular sheen that came from existing at frequencies reality barely acknowledged.
His lower body was covered in loose obsidian-gold pants that seemed to be woven from twilight itself.
The Goad rested beside him, that simple stick that could educate existence itself about its own nature!
Sigrid looked at him, then at their surroundings, her newly enhanced perception taking in details that should have been impossible to process!
Her eyes widened with recognition.
"Don’t tell me this... is an Early Veiled Shore?!"
The words emerged with the weight of someone recognizing they stood in a place that shouldn’t exist, that most beings would never even know could exist!
Early Veiled Shores were myth to most, legend to some, and death to nearly all who tried to reach them without proper understanding.
Noah walked up to them with confidence, his bare feet leaving perfect impressions in sand that remembered every step ever taken upon it.
"The one and only."
HUUM!
Titano’s reaction was more visceral. The giant’s head swiveled in all directions, trying to process everything at once.
He leaned down to touch the sand, letting the golden grains run through his massive fingers.
His eyes tracked to the crystalline waters that lapped at shores that extended into infinity!
The Aquarium with its impossible architecture. The trees bearing fruits that could elevate existence itself.
Then he saw them...the cluster of glass Woks that Noah had given him before, each one still filled with the soup of vibrant Marine Lifeforms. They sat arranged neatly near one of the trees!
Titano looked at all of this, his gaze moving back and forth between Noah and the wonders around them. His mouth opened and closed repeatedly, but words wouldn’t form!
He pointed at everything with an expression of amazement and shock that transcended his simple nature.
For once, the giant who could wrestle Inevitabilities into submission was completely speechless.
Noah smiled and patted his massive back, the gesture requiring him to reach up considerably.
"Come on, Brother. Let me introduce you to some people."
Noah kept things very straightforward and simple!
They moved toward the center of the Shore, where a gathering had naturally formed.
Amelia Osmont stood with a particular dignity. Henry was beside her, his complexity still surging from giving away his Everything of Fear.
The Emperor Penguin waddled about with self-importance that seemed comical until one remembered he had helped build an Abode.
Liora, Kazuhiko, Erikson, and others had assembled or were already nearby.
Noah brought the gigantic Titano over first, his massive form casting shadows that existed in multiple dimensions.
"Mother," Noah said with warmth, "this is Titano, an adopted brother I’ve taken on."
Titano, showing surprising grace for his size, bent down and extended one massive finger for Amelia to shake.
His simple mind was buzzing as even this simple interaction...being called a Brother...was something he never had during all the years with Duke Gwendolyn.
Honored Living Existences and lesser ones feared him.
Dukes looked at him like a chess piece. Nobody...had called him Brother!
Nobody had done what his brother was doing for him now!
So he put his massive finger out while making sure in his sinple thoughts that he would not cry.
Titano did not cry!
Amelia Osmont took his massive finge with the calm acceptance of someone who had long ago stopped being surprised by her son’s choices in companions.
But her eyes weren’t on the giant. They had fixed on Sigrid, who stood slightly behind, still processing everything she was witnessing.
Amelia’s expression shifted to something knowing, something that mothers throughout existence would recognize.
"Did you already find another daughter-in-law for me? How are you managing to do this on top of everything else?" she asked with a smile that contained layers of amusement. "Which one is this?"
WAA!

The wall that stops a child is merely a step for an adult.
The ocean that drowns a man is home to a fish.
The void that kills most beings is where others are born.

This wasn’t merely difficult or dangerous; it was deemed impossible.

Everyone knew this.

chapters.title: Chapter 4046: Variation! II
paragraphs: The question landed in the space between them as it carried devastating implications!
Sigrid’s mouth opened in shock, her gaze snapping to Noah with intensity that could have reorganized matter.
Another daughter-in-law? The word ‘another’ echoed in her mind. How many women did he have? Was she the second? The third? More?
In her dazed state, wrestling with revelations about Noah’s romantic situation while simultaneously processing that she stood in an Early Veiled Shore, Sigrid forgot to respond.
The silence stretched until Titano, with his characteristic simplicity, found his voice.
“Mother of Brother, this is Brother’s baddie, Sigrid, THE Living Order!”
The words emerged with such innocent certainty that their impact took a moment to fully register.
The Emperor Penguin raised his beak in shock.
Others could feel the terrifting Complexity surging within Sigrid as they did not even know what to think!
Brother’s baddie.
THE Living Order, one of the foundational forces of existence, a being whose return had just caused panic across a Transcendent Folds...referred to as someone’s ‘baddie’.
Any Living Origins, especially Duke Gwendolyn, would have been dismayed beyond recovery if they had heard such casual disrespect.
They would have blown their existences apart rather than accept such diminishment of what THE Living Order represented!
Amelia Osmont simply smiled wider.
“Is that right?”

The acceptance in those three words was absolute. If her son had somehow acquired THE Living Order as a companion, even if she did not fully know what that meant, then that was simply another day in her son’s weavings of Existence.
Sigrid’s mind snapped back to focus at this casual acceptance of the impossible.
Her eyes flashed sharply as she looked at Noah, her expression promising a conversation later that would involve many questions and possibly some educational violence.
He had a stick to educate, she had hands!

But for now, she moved forward with the grace that Order itself possessed. She took Amelia’s hands with genuine respect, her expression softening as she spoke a single word that would reshape reality around them.
“Mother.”
Mother.
Simple.
A single word that held many meanings and complexities!
A single word to change many things.
BOOM!

The word had barely left her lips when existence itself responded. Swirls of Living Order Authority erupted around Amelia Osmont’s form like reality recognizing something that should have always been true.
Prompts cascaded before Noah’s vision right after!
|The Mother of The Early Creature, Osmont, has been distinguished by THE Living Order|
|New Distinction Granted: Primordial Matriarch of Order’s Chosen|
|Amelia Osmont’s existence is undergoing fundamental correction|
|As the mother of the one who guides Living Existences and is chosen by Order itself, her being must slowly reflect this status|
|Complexity increasing: +100,000,000 per second for next 60 seconds. Slow gradual increase thereafter.|
|Purity increasing: +100,000,000 per second for next 60 seconds. Slow gradual increase thereafter.|
|Permanent passive increase: All future gains multiplied by 1000%|
|Authority granted: Can bless others with Order’s Favor (once per day)|
Noah watched this transformation with a smile that contained satisfaction beyond simple happiness.
His mother, who had supported him through impossibility itself, was finally receiving rewards that matched her significance.
“Okay,” he said, his perception expanding to encompass the entire Shore, “let’s see the rest.”
He asked to see the rest!
Because he could sense it...the Early Veiled Shore itself was responding to Sigrid’s presence.
From the moment THE Living Order had arrived, the space had been buzzing with potential that demanded expression. Now it exploded with glorious incandescence and torrents of information.
White light of Order bathed the golden sands, transforming them into something that transcended simple beach. Each grain reorganized itself according to principles that predated chaos!
|Fundamental Shore Evolution Ongoing. Your Shore is deviating from the normal growth of established Early Veiled Shores|
|All Early Veiled Shores originated from THE Creature and THE Living Existences|
|At moment of initial design, THE Living Order’s authority was absent|
|Order was not present when Early Veiled Shores were first forged|
|Order has bloomed inside an Early Veiled Shore for the first time|
|Unfathomable changes with incalculable effects are unfolding!|
|Due to Order’s inclusion, Shore features are being optimized and expanded|
|New Feature Unlocked: The Primordial Early Excavation Depths- Dimensional mines extending into collapsed fragments of the Earliest Folds|
|Access Requirement: Shore inhabitant with 100+ Million Complexity|
|Contents include remnants from the Earliest Folds and Desiccated Sleeping Shores|
|Available Resources:|
|Ore of Early Resonance|
- A Unique ore from the Earliest Folds
- Uses: Upgrading Shore constructs (Abode, Aquarium, etc.)
- Can be refined into Complexity Ingots (1 ingot = 100M CQ/PQ when consumed)
|Crystalized Temporal Fragments|
- Solidified time from before time was separated from space
- Uses: Accelerate plant maturation (1 fragment = 100 years instantly)
- Can be powdered and added to soil for permanent growth acceleration
|Memory Stones|
- Crystallized memories of deceased Early Creatures
- Uses: Gain random techniques, memories, understanding from the Earliest Folds
- Risk: 10% chance of temporary memory displacement
|Essence Gems|
- Pure crystallized complexity and purity
- Immediate consumption: +1 Billion CQ/PQ per gem
- Can be dissolved in Shore waters to call in Eminent and Kleos Early Living Marine Lifeforms
|Paradox Minerals|
- Ore that exists and doesn’t exist simultaneously
- Uses: Create items that function beyond normal limitations
- Can forge tools that work in Doorways to the Loom
|Structural Marrow|
- The bones of reality from before reality had bones
- Uses: Enhance Shore defenses to near-absolute levels
- Can be ground into powder that permanently increases toughness
Noahs eyes blazed at the overload of prompts as there was so much!
And each one was a work of wonder as before one could even fully focus on them, more came!
|Mining Mechanics within the Primordial Early Excavation Depths:|
- Infinite depth with increasing rewards per level
- Enemies: Remnant Lifeforms from collapsed Shores(May be Living, may be Dead, or in between)
- Environmental hazards that test existence itself
- Party system: Up to 5 beings can mine together for a greater chance of locating ores, crystals...
- Chance to find complete Early Creature artifacts
|Current Mine Levels Available: 1-100|
|Deeper levels unlock as Shore continues evolving|

chapters.title: Chapter 4047: Losses! I
paragraphs: Noah read through the extensive information with eyes that grew brighter with each detail.
This feature was an entire avenue of advancement, a way to gather resources that shouldn’t exist anymore!
Off to the side of the Shore, the space began to ripple and tear with purpose, like reality making room for something that needed to exist.
A massive arched entrance emerged from the sand, carved from stone that predated the concept of stone itself.
The archway was embedded with glimmering stones that cast light in colors of utter glory, each one a fragment from the Earliest Folds.
The entrance to the Primordial Early Excavation Depths stood there as if it had always existed, as if the Shore had simply been waiting for Order to arrive before revealing this secret.
Noah looked at Sigrid with an expression that mixed affection with amazement.
She was like a good luck charm of impossible proportions...her mere presence causing explosions of advancement and opportunity.
“Brother!” Titano’s voice boomed with excitement that could have powered small civilizations. “Brother’s home is... is... BROTHER’S HOME IS AMAZING!”
HUUM!
The giant had finally found his full faculty of words, and they emerged with the pure enthusiasm of someone who had discovered a glorious place exists and he had been invited to stay.
Around them, the inhabitants of the Shore were beginning to notice the new feature.
Emperor Penguin was already waddling toward the mine entrance with the certainty of someone who intended to be first. Kazuhiko’s hand was on his sword.
The Queen of Matter had her body buzzing like a beverage that would soon explode as she tried her best not to ruin the moment by screaming out!

But Noah’s attention remained on Sigrid, who was still processing everything...the Shore, its inhabitants, becoming his mother’s daughter-in-law through a single word, and now the transformation of the entire space through her mere presence.
“Welcome home,” he said to her, and meant it in ways that transcended the simple meaning of the words.
Because this wasn’t just a common shore anymore.
With Order’s presence, with Sigrid’s arrival, it had become something greater. Something that could grow beyond what THE Creature had originally envisioned.
The Early Veiled Shore had evolved, and with it, the possibilities for what Noah could become expanded toward infinity.
Noah absorbed all the wonders occurring around him, his consciousness expanding to process information.
|Due to Order’s inclusion, the Early Veiled Shore will undergo continuous transformation|
|Process will continue until reaching quantifiable conclusion for optimal advancement path|
|Estimated time to stabilization: 5-10 days|
|Unexpected evolutions possible during transition period|
He reflected on this calmly, his mind already calculating implications and possibilities. The timing was fortuitous...forced, perhaps, by circumstance, but fortuitous nonetheless.
“The Paradoxes and Origins should be in a standoff right about now,” he said, “I don’t see the Paradoxes making any grand moves before the Kleos Concordat.”
He gazed across his Shore, watching his people look towards the new mine entrance with varying degrees of excitement and caution.
“We can track our progression here and relax while we wait for the dust to settle.”
Sigrid nodded respectfully towards Amelia Osmont, though her expression carried concern as she turned. “Duke Gwendolyn and the others won’t give you too much trouble?”
The question carried layers...concern for his safety, understanding of existence, and awareness that her awakening had disrupted carefully maintained balances.
Noah’s smile held confidence that transcended arrogance. “I can handle it.”
WAA!
The simple statement carried such certainty that Sigrid nodded without hesitation. She believed him completely!

“The Early Veiled Shore has much to be done within it,” Noah continued, his gaze sweeping across his domain. “The plants are maturing, only waiting is required now. Marine Lifeforms are being caught continuously in the Aquarium. And to pass time while the Living Origins and Paradoxes scatter until the Kleos Concordat...”
He gestured toward the newly formed mine entrance as the Emperor Penguin was already arguing with Kazuhiko about who would enter first...when neither had met the Complexity requirement!
“The new feature of mining seems to be a good one to explore.”

His gaze returned to Sigrid, studying her with intensity that saw beyond surface. “We also have to see just how far your complexity will continue to rise. With me guiding you, your full awakening as THE Living Order should take... less than seven days.”
The seven days versus the one thousand years it would have taken without his guidance. The power of THE Living Existential Guider made manifest in simple mathematics!

Sigrid’s response bypassed words entirely. She moved forward with grace that made Order itself pay attention, ignoring the gathered crowd of Noah’s people, and wrapped her arms around him in an embrace.
Her head rested against his chest, and through that contact, she felt the immense waves of complexity swirling within him...power that should have been chaotic but wasn’t.

There was order to his being, structure that existed not through rigid law but through conscious choice. It didn’t fight her raging Order...it complemented it, completed it, made her transformation feel less like violent change and more like coming home.

The golden sands of the Early Veiled Shore gleamed beneath the glorious light. Cerulean stellar waves of Early Sacred Waters lapped at shores that extended into infinity, their rhythm matching the heartbeat of existence itself.
On this day, THE Living Order had arrived in the Early Veiled Shore of The Early Creature, Osmont.
What this would become remained unwritten, but the potential made reality itself lean forward in anticipation!
In the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds, time had passed with the weight of failure pressing against consciousness.
Duke Gwendolyn and the others emerged from the Doorway with expressions that had moved past shock into something deeper...the ashen pallor of those who had confirmed the impossible.
The Young Miss, along with the one who had taken her and Titano, were truly gone. Not hidden, not displaced, but absent in ways that violated understanding.
Duke Whisker needed only to meet Duke Gwendolyn’s eyes to understand the completeness of their failure. His tiny features arranged themselves into a frown that carried the weight of eons.
Schrodinger observed all of this with his beggar’s smile, floating casually as if witnessing a mildly interesting play.
“You all seem to be experiencing a great loss,” he said with sympathy that contained too many layers to be genuine. “You know, I have another story that deals with Losses-”
“While we would love to listen to a story,” Duke Gwendolyn interrupted, her composure cracking under urgency, “we have to go-...!”
She never finished the sentence.
BOOM!
The smile vanished from Schrodinger’s face with speed that made its previous presence seem like illusion.
In the next moment, Existence itself began to shake!
Existential Trembling.
Oh!
Trembling!
The pressure that erupted from the beggar-like Duke transcended physical force or energetic overwhelming.
This was authority at its most glorious- the weight of something that existed so thoroughly that reality had to acknowledge it or break!
Altheon and Thessaly didn’t even have time to scream.
Their Origins buzzed with frequencies that shouldn’t exist, and consciousness fled rather than endure what was happening!
They slumped into unconsciousness with the mercy of minds protecting themselves from truths too large to process!
5/5 Keep the Magic Castles and Golden Tickets coming!

Emperor Penguin was already waddling toward the mine entrance with the certainty of someone who intended to be first.
Kazuhiko’s hand was on his sword.
The Queen of Matter had her body buzzing like a beverage that would soon explode as she tried her best not to ruin the moment by screaming out!

But Noah’s attention remained on Sigrid, who was still processing everything...the Shore, its inhabitants, becoming his mother’s daughter-in-law through a single word, and now the transformation of the entire space through her mere presence.
“Welcome home,” he said to her, and meant it in ways that transcended the simple meaning of the words.
Because this wasn’t just a common shore anymore.
With Order’s presence, with Sigrid’s arrival, it had become something greater.
Something that could grow beyond what THE Creature had originally envisioned.
The Early Veiled Shore had evolved, and with it, the possibilities for what Noah could become expanded toward infinity.
Noah absorbed all the wonders occurring around him, his consciousness expanding to process information.
|Due to Order’s inclusion, the Early Veiled Shore will undergo continuous transformation|
|Process will continue until reaching quantifiable conclusion for optimal advancement path|
|Estimated time to stabilization: 5-10 days|
|Unexpected evolutions possible during transition period|
He reflected on this calmly, his mind already calculating implications and possibilities.
The timing was fortuitous...forced, perhaps, by circumstance, but fortuitous nonetheless.
“The Paradoxes and Origins should be in a standoff right about now,” he said, “I don’t see the Paradoxes making any grand moves before the Kleos Concordat.”
He gazed across his Shore, watching his people look towards the new mine entrance with varying degrees of excitement and caution.
“We can track our progression here and relax while we wait for the dust to settle.”
Sigrid nodded respectfully towards Amelia Osmont, though her expression carried concern as she turned.
“Duke Gwendolyn and the others won’t give you too much trouble?”
The question carried layers...concern for his safety, understanding of existence, and awareness that her awakening had disrupted carefully maintained balances.
Noah’s smile held confidence that transcended arrogance.
“I can handle it.”
WAA!
The simple statement carried such certainty that Sigrid nodded without hesitation.
She believed him completely!
“The Early Veiled Shore has much to be done within it,” Noah continued, his gaze sweeping across his domain.
“The plants are maturing, only waiting is required now.
Marine Lifeforms are being caught continuously in the Aquarium.
And to pass time while the Living Origins and Paradoxes scatter until the Kleos Concordat...”
He gestured toward the newly formed mine entrance as the Emperor Penguin was already arguing with Kazuhiko about who would enter first...when neither had met the Complexity requirement!
“The new feature of mining seems to be a good one to explore.”
His gaze returned to Sigrid, studying her with intensity that saw beyond surface.
“We also have to see just how far your complexity will continue to rise.
With me guiding you, your full awakening as THE Living Order should take... less than seven days.”
The seven days versus the one thousand years it would have taken without his guidance.
The power of THE Living Existential Guider made manifest in simple mathematics!
Sigrid’s response bypassed words entirely.
She moved forward with grace that made Order itself pay attention, ignoring the gathered crowd of Noah’s people, and wrapped her arms around him in an embrace.
Her head rested against his chest, and through that contact, she felt the immense waves of complexity swirling within him...power that should have been chaotic but wasn’t.
There was order to his being, structure that existed not through rigid law but through conscious choice.
It didn’t fight her raging Order...it complemented it, completed it, made her transformation feel less like violent change and more like coming home.
The golden sands of the Early Veiled Shore gleamed beneath the glorious light.
Cerulean stellar waves of Early Sacred Waters lapped at shores that extended into infinity, their rhythm matching the heartbeat of existence itself.
On this day, THE Living Order had arrived in the Early Veiled Shore of The Early Creature, Osmont.
What this would become remained unwritten, but the potential made reality itself lean forward in anticipation!
In the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds, time had passed with the weight of failure pressing against consciousness.
Duke Gwendolyn and the others emerged from the Doorway with expressions that had moved past shock into something deeper...the ashen pallor of those who had confirmed the impossible.
The Young Miss, along with the one who had taken her and Titano, were truly gone.
Not hidden, not displaced, but absent in ways that violated understanding.
Duke Whisker needed only to meet Duke Gwendolyn’s eyes to understand the completeness of their failure.
His tiny features arranged themselves into a frown that carried the weight of eons.
Schrodinger observed all of this with his beggar’s smile, floating casually as if witnessing a mildly interesting play.
“You all seem to be experiencing a great loss,” he said with sympathy that contained too many layers to be genuine.
“You know, I have another story that deals with Losses-”
“While we would love to listen to a story,” Duke Gwendolyn interrupted, her composure cracking under urgency, “we have to go-...!”
She never finished the sentence.
BOOM!
The smile vanished from Schrodinger’s face with speed that made its previous presence seem like illusion.
In the next moment, Existence itself began to shake!
Existential Trembling.
Oh!
Trembling!
The pressure that erupted from the beggar-like Duke transcended physical force or energetic overwhelming.
This was authority at its most glorious- the weight of something that existed so thoroughly that reality had to acknowledge it or break!
Altheon and Thessaly didn’t even have time to scream.
Their Origins buzzed with frequencies that shouldn’t exist, and consciousness fled rather than endure what was happening!
They slumped into unconsciousness with the mercy of minds protecting themselves from truths too large to process!
5/5 Keep the Magic Castles and Golden Tickets coming!

chapters.title: Chapter 4048: Losses! II
paragraphs: Even the Dukes, beings who stood at pinnacles of their respective hierarchies...turned ashen.
Their bodies shook with the simple struggle to maintain coherence against pressure that suggested they might be less real than what pressed against them!
Only Duke Whisker remained still, though the effort required was visible in how his stellar eyes blazed brighter, how his tiny form seemed to grow denser to resist dissolution.
Duke Gwendolyn’s paradoxical body buzzed and trembled, caught between states as if unable to decide whether existing was worth the effort required.
The beggar-looking Schrodinger had maintained his smile through everything...through threats, through confrontation, through games of power and position.
But when he had wanted to tell a story and been interrupted, denied his simple pleasure of narrative, the atmosphere transformed completely!
He alone, facing a dozen Dukes of Origins, caused all nearby Existence to tremble. Everyone felt stifled, compressed, made aware of their own insignificance.

Duke Whisker, with effort that made space crack around him, floated forward to position himself before the other Origins. His voice emerged with grim calmness that acknowledged the precipice they balanced upon.
“We should have time for another story before we leave.”
The statement wasn’t a suggestion.
Schrodinger held his cold gaze for several more seconds, letting them marinate in the understanding of what they had almost provoked.

Then, as suddenly as it had arrived, the pressure vanished. His harmless beggar appearance returned, complete with gentle smile, as if the Existential Trembling had been nothing more than shared hallucination.
“Well then,” he said pleasantly, “let me tell you about Loss.”
He settled into the air as if it were a comfortable chair, his posture suggesting he had all the time that had ever existed.

“I was moving across the Earliest Folds...this was before I understood what I would become, when I was still discovering what paradox meant. I was chasing something magnificent: a shattered fragment of an Early Veiled Shore.”
His eyes grew distant with memory that might have been real or might have been constructed for effect.

“Imagine it...a piece of those sacred spaces, broken off and drifting through the Folds like a boat without anchor. The potential contained within even a fragment... it could have elevated me beyond measure. So I chased it with dedication that bordered on madness.”
He paused, ensuring his audience was properly captured. He blinked on Duke Whisker, Valen, and Gwendolyn as he continued!

“During this chase, I encountered an Inevitability. But this one didn’t attack. It seemed... curious about what I was doing. It floated alongside me, making sounds that might have been questions in languages that hadn’t been invented yet.”
Schrodinger’s expression grew rueful.

“But I was at a pivotal moment. The fragment was within reach...almost. Just a little more effort, a little more focus, and it would be mine. So I dismissed this curious Inevitability. Ignored it completely. Why did I care for some paradoxical observer when transcendence was within grasp?”
He shook his head at his younger self’s foolishness.

“I chased for a day and a night. Through spaces that existed sideways to reality. Through moments that happened before and after simultaneously. And then... I lost sight of it. The fragment simply vanished, as if it had never existed at all.”
The silence that followed carried weight.

“As I floated there in my failure, wondering how I had lost something I had been so close to claiming, I heard a voice. It buzzed through all existence, making reality itself tremble with recognition.”
Schrodinger’s voice shifted, taking on waves that suggested something vast speaking through constrained form:

“‘I, THE Living Concept, tried to embody an Inevitability to meet worthy creatures of the Folds. To see who might recognize thought itself wearing paradox as costume. And you actually ignored me, chasing something that was never meant to be yours.'”
He returned to his normal voice, though the weight of the memory remained.
“‘What a loss,’ THE Living Concept had said that day. ‘What a loss!'”
Schrodinger looked at each of the Living Origins, his gaze lingering on Duke Gwendolyn with particular weight.

“So you see, I know something about heavy losses. About something slipping right past your fingers while you chase what seemed more important.” His smile contained sympathy that might have been genuine.
“It is okay. We all have our stories of what escaped us while we weren’t paying attention to what mattered.”
The silence that followed was immense.

No one dared speak, each processing the implications of the story...that Schrodinger had once been noticed by THE Living Concept, that he had missed such an opportunity through narrow focus, that losses could be teachers if one survived them!
Finally, Schrodinger nodded with the air of someone ending a satisfactory visit.
“Alright, you all get going now. We shall see each other soon enough at the Kleos Concordat.”
The dismissal was gentle but absolute.
Duke Gwendolyn, Whisker, and the others began moving toward the white-gold portal with the careful movements of people backing away from something dangerous.

Duke Valen remained a moment longer, his blind eyes seeing things others couldn’t. He shook his head with a smile that contained layers of meaning, a gesture toward Schrodinger that might have been acknowledgment, warning, or simple amusement.
Then he too disappeared.

The encirclement of Living Paradoxes remained perfectly still, hundreds of impossible beings maintaining positions with patience that transcended time. Only after the last Origin had vanished did movement return, and then only slightly.
Diviticus approached Schrodinger with uncharacteristic hesitation, her usual confidence cracked by what she had witnessed.
“Sir,” she said carefully, “when will we put the Corpse into use?”
Schrodinger didn’t even glance at her, his gaze fixed on something beyond normal perception. “Everything is in due time. Everything.”
Everything.
The repetition of ‘Everything’ seemed to trigger something in him.

He raised his hand, studying its callouses with the intensity of someone reading fate in skin patterns. His mind drifted to memories older than most civilizations...to the first of his Everything that he had given away.
The memory made him smile with genuine warmth that transformed his beggar’s face into something almost paternal.
“Everything,” he repeated once more, but this time the word contained multitudes.

chapters.title: Chapter 4049: Sir! I
paragraphs: In the distance, the white rays of Order finally began to fade from the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds, leaving only normal impossibility in their wake. But the changes those rays had initiated, the transformations they had catalyzed, those would continue rippling through existence!
It would be known across the Folds.
Order...had returned!
The Kleos Concordat approached, and with it, convergences that would reshape many things
But for now, there was only waiting. And stories. And the memory of Everythings... given and received!

Perception shapes reality in ways that transcend the physical. How one believes they are perceived by others can transform their entire mental landscape, creating prisons or palaces from nothing more than assumption.
Some walk through existence crushed beneath imagined judgment.
They believe others see them as strange, inadequate, unworthy.

This perception becomes a weight that bends their shoulders, dims their voice, makes them smaller with each passing day. Anxiety blooms from seeds that were never planted, depression grows from soil that exists only in their minds!

Others stride forward wrapped in assumed admiration. They believe themselves seen as intelligent, confident, capable. This perception becomes armor and wings simultaneously, carrying them through challenges that might break those who doubt.
They act calm because they believe others expect calmness. They project confidence because they assume it’s already attributed to them.
The anxious do not know that they can always choose to do the same. To simply project confidence and calmness as this...would change their lives immensely!
Across existence, perception determines trajectories. Wars have been fought over how nations believed they were viewed.
Loves have died from assumptions about what a glance meant.
Entire civilizations have risen or fallen based on how they thought history would remember them!
But...there was one being who cared remarkably little for how others perceived him.
In Aeternitas Concordia, Noah’s merchant body remained in the domed garden with the tranquility of someone tending their own backyard.

He examined the plants with genuine interest, though he noted they weren’t as terrifying as the ones he had planted in his Shore. These were domesticated things, powerful but tamed, lacking the raw potential of truly wild growth.
His contemplation shattered as the garden suddenly buzzed and shook with the force of multiple arrivals.
Duke-level Living Origins materialized in rapid succession, their combined presence making reality pay attention!
But it was Duke Gwendolyn whose fury blazed brightest, her eyes locking onto Noah with intensity that could have melted lesser beings.

She hauled the still-unconscious bodies of Thessaly and Altheon like sacks of grain, dumping them unceremoniously as her focus remained fixed on him. When she spoke, her voice cracked with barely controlled rage.
“Where is she?!”
The question rang through the garden with force that made the tamed plants tremble.

Every Duke present immediately understood...somehow, impossibly, this merchant was the one who had taken what they had gone to retrieve from the Transcendent Paradoxical Folds. THE Living Order had vanished under his influence!

A dozen Dukes of Living Origins fixed their gazes upon him. Each stare carried enough weight to crush Prime Living Existences into paste. The combined pressure of their attention should have been unbearable, should have forced him to his knees or worse.
Noah bore it without flinching.
After all, he had moved through an Existential Trembling. This was merely... attention.
He looked at Duke Gwendolyn with the same calm he’d shown while examining plants. When he spoke, his voice carried no stress, no acknowledgment of the pressure bearing down upon him.
“She is safe. Somewhere where she cannot be threatened by Paradoxes, Inevitabilities... or anything else.” He paused, his gaze drifting away from Gwendolyn though his words remained clearly directed.
“And best of all, nobody knows where. So nobody cannot just blab away everything about her.”
The accusation landed with precision that made Duke Gwendolyn’s nature flare visibly.

“You...!” Power pulsed from her form, the might of a Duke making space crack around her edges. “The Living Order is not yours to take and make decisions for! She belongs to and with the Living Origins! For you to come in here and do all this... just who do you think you-”
WU!
Before she could finish, brilliant authority erupted from Duke Whisker. The tiny mouse’s power vibrated through existence with such force that reality itself considered trembling.
Almost trembled. The fact that it only almost happened made the display more terrifying than if it had fully manifested.
Duke Gwendolyn’s words died instantly. Her nostrils flared, fists clenched white, as she continued staring at Noah with fury that had no outlet.
Duke Whisker’s ancient gaze moved across the assembled Dukes before settling on Noah with weight that transcended simple observation.
“Leave us,” he said to the others. “I will ascertain things here.”
Several Dukes shifted, clearly wanting to object. They were Dukes...who was Whisker to dismiss them like subordinates?
The answer came as the small mouse’s body began radiating terrifying white light. Not of Origin, but of Beginning itself...something more fundamental, more absolute.
The other Dukes found themselves moving toward the exits without conscious decision, their bodies obeying before their minds could object!
Duke Whisker clearly held a unique position among the Dukes of Living Origins, one that transcended simple seniority or power.

Duke Valen left with a knowing nod, his blind eyes seeing more than sight allowed. Duke Gwendolyn was the last to depart, her reluctance visible in every movement, but even she couldn’t resist that white light of Beginning.
When the garden held only Noah and the tiny Duke, the atmosphere shifted completely.
Duke Whisker studied Noah for a long moment. Then the somber tension he had been radiating dissolved, replaced by something almost conversational!
He breathed out, a surprisingly human gesture from such a form, and spoke with calm certainty.
“Sir, I apologize for how your interactions with Living Origins have gone so far.”
BOOM!
The word hit Noah with more force than any attack could have.
Sir.
A Duke of the Living Origins had called him ‘Sir.’
Noah’s composed expression buzzed slightly, genuine surprise showing through. “For what reason could you be calling me Sir?”
